paper_title: Finding a Highly Connected Steiner Subgraph and its Applications
classifications: Theory of computation → Parameterized complexity and exact algorithms
statement: There are several possible directions of future work. Our main result proves that Steiner Subgraph Extension is FPT when the removal of terminals results in a bounded degenerate graph. If is unclear if Steiner Subgraph Extension is FPT even when G − X is an arbitrary graph class and p is a fixed constant. Proving such a (positive or negative) result Steiner Subgraph Extension remains an interesting future work. If p = 2, then finding p-vertex/edge-connected steiner subgraph admits k O(k) nO(1) -time algorithm [19, 15]. It remains open if a 2-vertex-connected steiner subgraph can be obtained in 2O(k) nO(1) -time even when the set of terminals is a vertex cover of the input graph. On the perspective of applications of Theorem 1, we have been successful in designing singly exponential-time FPT algorithms for p-Edge-Con-BDDS, p-Edge-Con-η-TDDS, p-Edge-Con-PW1DS and p- Edge-Con-η-PVC.
